# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

[mp-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30408133/mp-repro.zip)

story.summary: Fixes a crash in the generator and analyzer when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic sites in `TypeCollector` no longer index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`; they use null-safe lookups instead. Separately, the analyzer's diagnostic callback is wrapped in a filter that drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source location inside the current compilation. Three new tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only reference, then check that the consumer builds with no diagnostics and that its resolver is generated. README and MsgPack004.md gain paragraphs describing the new reporting behaviour.
story.why: Metadata symbols have an empty `DeclaringSyntaxReferences`. Indexing `[0]` threw `IndexOutOfRangeException`, which killed the generator (CS8785) and the analyzer (AD0001). The assembly was then left with no generated resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global reporting filter (`ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, line 239 and lines 1436-1450). It silently drops every diagnostic with no in-compilation source location, including `Location.None` ones, not only those about metadata types.
README section and MsgPack004.md section documenting that consumers no longer see member diagnostics for referenced types.
The issue names three `[0]` sites (lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff changes only two of them. The third may be gone in this version or may still be present; this cannot be told from the diff.
story.confidence_overview: High that the two edited sites no longer throw for metadata properties. Medium that the new tests reproduce the original crash: the record-struct test mirrors the issue repro, but I cannot confirm the verifier runs the analyzer. Medium-low on the side effects of the broad reporting filter.

refusals.what: A global filter silently discards diagnostics without an in-compilation source location.
refusals.why: It goes beyond the crash fix and changes user-visible analyzer output for every type, including `Location.None` diagnostics on source types. A human should decide whether to drop these diagnostics or keep reporting them.

refusals.what: Documentation commits the project to a policy that member diagnostics for referenced types are never reported in the consuming project.
refusals.why: This is a product decision not asked for by the requirement.

refusals.what: The README advertises support for referenced generic value types and states the new diagnostic policy.
refusals.why: The added user-facing documentation commits to behaviour beyond the bug fix.

findings.description: The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source. That includes `Location.None`, which Roslyn permits analyzers to report. Any existing diagnostic for a source type whose location helper returns null (e.g. `GetIdentifierLocation`, `GetParameterListLocation`, or the new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` on a positional record property) will now disappear silently rather than surface. This is broader than needed to skip metadata members.

For a source record's positional property, the syntax is a `ParameterSyntax`, so the `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` cast yields null. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic is then filtered out entirely, where it previously crashed. No test covers line 985 at all.

The issue names three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (735, 1009, 1101). The diff changes only two. If an unguarded `[0]` remains in another `GetObjectInfo` diagnostic path, a different metadata shape could still crash. This cannot be confirmed from the diff.

The helper is built on the generator verifier (`CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator>`). It is not shown whether this runs `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`, so the AD0001 half of the bug may be untested.

Line 1076 still calls derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() without null-propagation right next to the fixed line 1077, and SyntaxNode.GetLocation() is an instance method. If a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly has a member (even a private one) with a custom KeyAttribute-derived attribute, its metadata AttributeData has no syntax reference, and because lines 1075-1077 evaluate eagerly before both the accessibility check and this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke, both the generator (CS8785) and analyzer (AD0001) will crash with NullReferenceException. In addition, REQ-2283 identified three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites in GetObjectInfo (original lines 735, 1009, 1101), and only two (985 and 1077) were updated.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic with Location.None (since Location.None.IsInSource is false), silently suppressing legitimate errors in the current compilation in at least two cases: (1) for a record positional property in source such as [MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key(null!)] string X), DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax() is a ParameterSyntax rather than a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (line 1434) returns null and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) is created with Location.None and dropped (as is any other source diagnostic whose location helper returns null, e.g. GetParameterListLocation on a null or synthesized method); and (2) when the consuming project closes a valid referenced generic struct Item<T> with an unformattable metadata type argument such as Item<System.Version>, neither Item<T>'s member nor System.Version has a syntax tree in the consuming compilation, so the error is dropped in the consumer while the defining assembly could not have reported it on open T either (contradicting README.md line 1642).

out_of_scope.description: The global `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filter (lines 239 and 1436-1450) changes which diagnostics reach users for all types, not just referenced ones.
New documentation section on generic types from referenced assemblies.
New documentation of the analyzer's reporting scope.
